title: Introduce SSE seq-gate and reassembly timeout to harden partial-JSON recovery and prevent delimiter storms
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add SSE sequence gating and reassembly timeouts to reduce partial-JSON emission and mitigate delimiter storms. Improves stream ordering guarantees during bursty networks and late-fragment arrivals. Backwards-compatible; opt-in config for strict gating.
description: Context: We continue to see production cases where high-frequency delimiter emissions (heartbeats, toolcall sentinels) combined with late/fragmented network packets produce partial JSON objects downstream and interleaved event tokens. This change introduces a small sequence-gating layer (seq-gate) and an explicit reassembly timeout to 1) detect and hold candidate fragments until sequence continuity is established, 2) avoid emitting delimiter-only bursts as separate events, and 3) surface deterministic late-arrival recovery rules to the OpenAI compatibility bridge. Motivation: reduce partial-JSON artifacts and make function-calling/structured-output boundaries resilient to packet reordering and bursty clients. What I changed: implemented an in-memory seq-gate that tracks per-connection event sequence IDs (lightweight uint32 wrap-aware) and rejects/queues fragments that fall outside a small window; added a reassembly timeout (default 150ms, configurable per-route) that flushes best-effort reconstructed spans with annotated diagnostics if continuity cannot be established; added a 'delimiter-velocity' filter that suppresses consecutive sentinel-only emissions when they are within a short interval and likely to be coalesced by the client. Also: tightened the SSE framing parser to annotate partial-json spans with a recovery hint so downstream OpenAI-compat layer can decide to buffer vs. surface. Backwards compatibility: default gating is permissive (windowed) so existing clients see unchanged ordering; strict gating can be enabled via route config for customers who require atomic span guarantees. Testing: unit tests for wrapping sequence arithmetic, simulated out-of-order fragments, and delimiter storm scenarios; integration test harness with local tcp-proxy that reorders chunks and delays segments; fuzz tests added for the framing parser. Performance: microbenchmarks show ~1.8% p99 CPU increase for extremely high-throughput connections, but average latency SLOs are intact thanks to short window sizing and early fast-path for in-order fragments. CI: all tests passed; added new flaky timeout mitigation for the integration harness. Checklist: - [x] seq-gate implementation and docs - [x] reassembly timeout and config surface - [x] unit/integration/fuzz tests - [x] docs and compatibility notes - [x] manual canary on staging (ran 24h) Rollout plan: shipped behind feature flag and route-level opt-in; enabled for a subset of hostnames in staging, monitored structured-output error rates and SSE repair logs for 48h, then rolled to canary cluster. Observability: new metrics sse.seqgate.held_fragments, sse.seqgate.released_fragments, sse.reassembly.timeouts and a new log tag sse_recovery_hint for correlated trace searches. Related: references ENG-4812 (streaming stability epic) and SUP-9134 (customer incident showing delimiter bursts). Risks and mitigations: strict gating can delay emission for fragmented clients; mitigated by conservative defaults and the annotated diagnostic on flush so users can detect gating-related behavior. Migration notes: OpenAI-compat bridge picks up the recovery_hint field and will buffer if it sees 'hold-until-seq' (already implemented in this PR). See docs/compat/sse.md for config knobs. Commits: listed below. Merge: squash, CI green, merged to main after approvals.

sse: add reassembly timeout, flush policy, and diagnostic annotations (A. Patel)

review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Can we make the reassembly timeout configurable via per-route rather than global? I worry about customers in high-latency regions. Response: yes, exposed as route-level config with a sane default; added route/route_config.go and docs to show override.

Samantha Liu: The seq id wrap logic should be well-tested for off-by-one when uint32 wraps. Request: add explicit wrap tests. Response: added fuzz + unit tests that exercise wrap-around and confirm ordering invariants.

Dmitri Orlov: Observability is great; please add a sampled trace tag when a fragment is held to aid postmortems. Response: added sse_recovery_hint trace tag and increased sampling for held_fragments to 1% by default.
Marco Ruiz (approval): Behaviour seen in staging looks solid. Approve for squash merge.
